newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil rebounds, French demand firms diesel.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil rebounds, French demand firms diesel.

text.p: NWE gas oil rebounded in late trade in line with benchmark futures and physical prices were notionally higher despite a dearth of buying interest in the heating oil market, traders said.
A national holiday in the key German market kept many buyers away, but underlying fundamentals were still sound with low stocks promising some heavy buying as end-users start to restock for winter.
U.S. 0.2 sulphur heating oil was at Nov IPE +$12/15 cif NWE for second half Oct delivery, while prompt Russian parcels were rumoured to have traded at quotes m/m flat, cif NWE.
Short-covering requirements into France for low sulphur diesel kept EN590 quotes firm with a second half Oct cargo traded at cif quotes high +$5 basis Bordeaux.
A refiner was offering a cargo into Le Havre at Oct IPE +$22 for deliovery before Oct 20, while offers on the barge market crept as high as Oct IPE +$20 fob ARA.
IPE Oct futures closed $3.50 up at $246 a tonne, after retracing earlier losses. The Oct/Nov backwardation widened a further 50 cents to $11.50.
